blocks.content: Manipur's environment chapter centres on the Sangai deer and Loktak Lake ecosystem introduced in Chapter 1, alongside its substantial forest cover and other protected areas across the hill districts.

The Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii, Manipur brown-antlered deer), Manipur's state animal, is found in the wild ONLY at Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake (Chapter 1) — making it one of the most geographically restricted large mammal populations in India, and a flagship species for the state's conservation efforts.

The Sangai is popularly called the 'Dancing Deer' of Manipur, a name derived from its distinctive, careful, high-stepping gait as it moves across the floating phumdi vegetation of its swampy habitat — appearing to 'dance' across the unstable floating ground.

The species was, at points in the 20th century, believed to be extinct in the wild before rediscovery and subsequent dedicated conservation efforts brought about a gradual, carefully monitored population recovery, making the Sangai's conservation story a notable case study in Indian wildlife-conservation history.

★ EXAM POINT: The Sangai = 'Dancing Deer', Manipur's state animal, found in the wild ONLY at Keibul Lamjao National Park — one of the most restricted-range large mammals in India, and a species that was at one point believed extinct in the wild before conservation-driven recovery.

cells: World's only floating national park; last wild habitat of the Sangai deer (Chapter 1)
Home to the Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae), a rare, endemic flower found nowhere else in the world, blooming in a brief seasonal window and celebrated at the annual Shirui Lily Festival
Notable protected forest area in the hill districts

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae), endemic to Shirui Kashong Peak in Ukhrul district, is found NOWHERE ELSE in the world — a frequently tested endemic-species fact, distinct from (but often paired with) the Sangai deer in Manipur environment questions.

items: Sangai deer ('Dancing Deer') = Manipur's state animal, found in the wild only at Keibul Lamjao National Park (Loktak Lake).
Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae) = endemic flower found only at Shirui Kashong Peak, Ukhrul district; celebrated at the Shirui Lily Festival.
Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary (Chandel district) is another notable protected area.
